The common choices are visible in its rail; More reports lists the remaining reports, and Look up holds Property, Owner, Data and definitions, Deposit schedule and Message history. Every report describes its population and date basis under its title. Refresh data, Export and print and Saved views are at the top right. Filters act on retained verified summaries; drafts do not become issued report actions. Reports is read-only: nothing in it changes a case.

    Report Principal date and counting basis
    Open cases by area Open on the selected as-of date after an issued notice or snow citation
    Cases by inspector Cases opened in the period, by case inspector and area
    Open violations by area Items still open on the as-of date after notice issuance
    All cases Cases opened by initial inspection date in the period, with current status
    All violations Non-withdrawn items on cases opened in the period
    Days to compliance Initial inspection to item correction; excludes snow cases
    Repeat cases by owner Two or more opened cases, grouped by usable owner mailing address
    Citations by ordinance Effective non-void citations issued in the period
    Overridden deposits Authorized exceptional determined deposits issued in the period
    Referrals for prosecution Referrals issued in the period, with owner facts as referred
    Document actions Effective issued actions in the period; includes scoped actions before a notice

    Use From/To for period reports and As of for historical open-state reports. Date shortcuts set the corresponding range. Open More filters for additional scope such as status, owner, violation type or ordinance. Applied-filter chips reveal active scope even when its control is collapsed. Reset filters returns to the current year, current district boundaries and unfiltered optional fields, and clears sorting.

    Click a sortable column heading to set its order. The active screen, CSV, matching workbook report sheet and print use the same stable row order. Other named workbook sheets retain their own definitions; do not assume every sheet uses a citation issue date merely because the active report does.

    Saved local views retain their report, dates, filters, map choice and sort. Relative local date choices recalculate on use. Shared views retain their established filter/date/map format without shared sort. Manual report switching clears the saved-view selection and old return notice while retaining the working filters and sort context.

    Owner grouping by mailing address can combine owners represented by the same manager; names are shown for interpretation. Citation tiers count effective issued history, not an external conviction feed. Document action counts can exceed visit counts because compatible actions can share one physical visit.

    17 Verify report coverage maps and exports

    Check coverage first. Open Data and definitions. Its Coverage and next actions card explains what to do about missing, stale or excluded summaries; expand Record proof and excluded files and Data definitions for the details. Review the read time, included case files and excluded summaries. Missing summaries, exact source-revision mismatches, earlier-format summaries, summaries not matching their verified case and unreadable or duplicate entries are explained separately. Categories can overlap; an unreadable-entry count is not a unique-case count. Do not add them together as a case total.

    Each included current summary must match the independently read case bytes and integrity proof, and its reported facts must equal what the verified case itself shows. A summary that names the current case revision but reports different facts (for example an owner, status, date, document, violation or citation) is excluded as not matching its case. A rebuild regenerates summaries from the verified cases; it does not repair altered case history or grant legal approval. An administrator should first resolve the underlying record issue, then use Tools & settings → Saved work & connection → Connection checks and technical details → Storage diagnostics → Rebuild reporting index. Refresh Reports and recheck the exclusions before relying on totals.

    Maps. Switch between table and map when the report supports a map. Select area/boundary and basemap choices deliberately. GIS enrichment depends on access to City services; records without a usable location remain disclosed. Use the map’s table alternative for the same report population and review unlocated records. A missing point is not evidence that a case was excluded from the report count.

    Drill into data. Open a count or case link to inspect its underlying cases. Open case in Writer continues its existing work in Writer. Back to Reports in the Writer rail returns to the open Reports tab, or opens Reports in this tab when none answers, and restores the report, filters, view, date mode and sort retained when the case was opened; relative date choices recalculate for today. Check dates and filters after a return or data refresh, especially when a source record has changed.

    Export. Expand Export and print at the top of the report. Current report — CSV contains exactly the rows and columns of this table, with its filters, dates and sort. Reports workbook — Excel contains an About sheet, record sheets (Cases, Violations, Visits, Citations, Referrals, Corrections) and a sheet for every named report, with numeric/date values where appropriate. Sheets do not all apply the filters the same way; the About sheet’s Sheet scope lists each one. Cases, Violations and Visits contain cases opened in the period; Visits lists every visit on those cases, so a visit date can fall outside the period. Citations and Referrals use the date issued on any counted case, and the inspector filter means the issuing or referring inspector; Citations does not apply the violation type filter. Corrections uses the date each correction was recorded, so it can list cases opened before the period. Violations applies violation type and ordinance to each item; other sheets apply them to the case (any matching item), except Citations, which applies the ordinance to the citation. Area, owner and status always apply to the case, and status is its current status. Numbered report sheets match each report on screen: reports 1 and 3 use the As of date, reports 2 and 4–7 the case opening date, and reports 8–11 the date issued. This report’s sheet keeps the table sort and other report sheets use their default order. Print uses the active report presentation. Check the title, date range, applied filters, row order and coverage statement before distributing an export. An invalid date range clears stale report results so an earlier table is not exported as the new request.

    Deposit schedule. The deposit explorer presents searchable human-readable rules, conditions, effective dates and source details. Pagination limits screen volume; it does not omit the retained schedule. A displayed row may be conditional or require an authorized manual amount. The explorer is not a new court policy. If a sort fails, the report displays its default order and a notice; review the active order again before distributing an export. A malformed helper response reports its HTTP status and asks you to refresh or contact IT rather than showing an unreadable response as current report data.

    Refresh speed. The helper overlaps a maximum of four read-only file operations per request while retaining independent revision and integrity checks. Allow a shared read to finish before treating its coverage as current. Actual City cold/warm performance, history volume, simultaneous users and budget approval still require measurement.

    18 Use planning tools and display controls

    Tools & settings groups actions by purpose. Cases & planning contains Reminders and Batch draft due dates. Saved work & connection and Open saved case handle persistence; Exit Document Writer, in the same group, stops the program on this computer (see chapter 1). Program instructions opens this manual and its printable PDF. Display & help contains theme, message history and keyboard shortcuts. Administrator tools, collapsed at the end, contains Review catalog, Administrator deposit override and Review snow-letter content; each keeps its own administrator checks, and the grouping grants no authorization. Saved work & connection, Message history and Keyboard shortcuts open as dialogs over the screen; Close returns you.

    Reminders. Configure the intended reminder period and enabled state. Workspace exposes applicable reminder actions. Draft a reminder, inspect the recipient and wording, and complete the Outlook sending step separately. Reminders do not change a due date, prove service or create a new inspection. Snow items have no ordinary deadline reminder.

    Batch draft due dates. Select eligible unissued notice drafts and the required deadline, then apply it deliberately. Review each resulting draft. This updates private draft deadlines; it does not amend an issued notice. Ordinary outstanding-item date limits and snow exclusions remain enforced. Use the correction workflow for issued deadlines.

    Open saved case. Select a case-record export when appropriate. It is different from a workspace backup and does not contain every private form or worksheet. Opening it still respects current shared state and identity safeguards.

    Display. Under Color theme choose Use device setting, Light, Dark or High contrast. Use device setting follows the browser or operating system setting. Reduced-motion preferences remove nonessential transitions. Theme changes affect the screen; issued document print bodies retain their established appearance.

    Messages. Warning and error messages clear after 15 seconds; read them before they clear, or open Message history, which keeps cleared and dismissed messages for review. A dismissed notification does not mean a pending save or PDF job has completed. Keyboard help is available here and through ? outside an editable field.

    Administrative deposit exceptions. Only an operator acting under actual division authority should use Administrator deposit override. Open it from Tools & settings → Administrator tools. Supply the actual named administrator, reason, source and required confirmation. The helper records authorization and Reports exposes overridden deposits. This does not change the master schedule, establish court authority or approve unrelated citations.

    Keep technical diagnostics with the administrator. Avoid putting passwords, operational personal data or whole case folders in casual support messages. Provide the specific safe error code, time and approved log excerpt needed to investigate.

    19 Administer configuration integrity and maintenance

    Use the division’s IT and policy owners for changes. Deploy configuration as a coordinated release or through the program’s explicit shared administration workflows. Do not edit live JSON histories or generated HTML to work around a check.

    Shared folders. Program files are read-only for inspectors. Case JSON Files, Documents To Be Mailed And Recorded and Reporting GIS need the intended helper read/write access. Restrict Case JSON Files_administration to authorized administrators while allowing the reads required by inspectors. Keep integrity settings and the independent anchor under IT control.

    Protected anchor. The anchor is outside the case folder and reachable by every inspector PC. IT supplies integrity-settings.json locally on each PC and protects the configuration through its approved administration procedure; the launcher never copies that file from the share, including when no local file exists. IT configures append/create-only anchor access without modify/delete and verifies the actual NTFS/share behavior. The case-folder registry alone provides only partial tamper protection. Keep anchor backups and permissions with the records recovery plan.

    Record holds. A damaged migration registry or outside-edited case is an incident, not a reason to run an index rebuild repeatedly. Preserve the file, registry, retained PDFs and independent evidence. Inspectors use read-only review. Administrators use the documented offline integrity tooling only after establishing the trusted source and approved recovery plan.

    Locks. Inspect a case lock shows diagnostic information. Age alone never establishes abandonment, particularly on a remote PC. Do not delete lock files manually. Coordinate the owning client, confirm its state and use the token-bound recovery procedure only when the required evidence permits it.

    Approved connections. The release contains trusted-connections.json. GIS URLs must use HTTPS on an approved host; the defaults are maps.cityofmadison.com and opendata.arcgis.com. Credentials, HTTP/file URLs, unapproved ports and responses above 20 MB are refused, and redirects must stay on the approved host. The report server for the live import is named only by the release allowlist (shipped: entreports.cityofmadison.com); the shared folder cannot name another. Allowlist changes are made by the release owner in a new release, not through share settings.

    Live reports. Case lookup and the open-case lists read the division’s DocumenGeneratorImport and OpenEnforcementCases_BI reports from the City report server as XML, with each person’s own Windows sign-in; no password or credential is stored, and the report server’s certificate is always validated. Shared Case Lookup/settings.json accepts only enabled (the server and database keys of earlier releases are ignored). The report owner maintains the report queries; their names, parameters and column names must stay the same. See CASE-LOOKUP-GUIDE.md for the report setup and error codes.

    Policy and catalog. Record actual authority for language approval, new scoped documents, pricing exceptions and seasonal content. Mandatory defendant instructions need a separately approved source and release integration. Existing supplied pricing-date and snow-default questions remain policy decisions, not automatically approved by this release.

    Retention. Retain case events, migration evidence, anchor receipts and exact original PDF operation receipts according to approved records policy. The program does not compact or delete them. Future compaction requires records approval and proof of archived-byte retrieval and interruption recovery before implementation.

    Release ownership. Only the release owner writes to the deployment folder’s program files; inspectors have read-only access there. The release owner builds each release with the complete gate (tools/verify_release.py, then tools/package_release.py), publishes the deploy ZIP’s SHA-256 through a separate trusted channel, and keeps the previous complete release for deliberate rollback. IT records the folder permissions in the acceptance record.

    Connection and deployment

    Install the entire deploy folder as described in Start Document Writer - READ ME.md, stop the running program (Exit Document Writer in Tools & settings; for an older version without it, close its command window or sign out of Windows), and double-click the Document Writer icon again. Confirm the build and helper versions match the install guide. The launcher requires case_lookup.py, inspector_cases.py, ssrs_reports.py and ssrs_fetch.ps1 in addition to the prior core runtime. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is used; no SQL client, ODBC driver or additional Python package is installed. City script-signing/application-control policies still apply. IT should approve or sign the delivered script through its normal process if required; the launcher does not bypass those policies.

    The live data comes from two reports published on the City report server entreports.cityofmadison.com, in /Prod/Local/Building Inspection/Enforcement/:

    • DocumenGeneratorImport (parameter CaseNumber): one case’s property, owner and every inspection, for Find Case Inspections and for a selected open case.
    • OpenEnforcementCases_BI (parameter Inspector): the open enforcement cases. Rendered without a parameter it lists every inspector’s cases, which the helper counts for the inspector list; one inspector’s cases are rendered with the name exactly as the report printed it.

    Each report is rendered as XML (rs:Format=XML) by Windows PowerShell with the signed-in user’s Windows sign-in (-UseDefaultCredentials). No password, credential or connection string is stored, and each person sees only what their own account may open in the Reports portal. The computer must be on the City network, directly or through VPN. The report server comes only from the verified release (trusted-connections.json); the report paths are fixed in the program. The only values sent are a validated case number or an inspector name taken from the report’s own list, URL-encoded. The report owner (the division) owns the report queries, including the open-case rule; a change saved to a report applies at once, without a new release, as long as its name, parameters and column names stay the same.

    The shared Case Lookup/settings.json has one setting: {"enabled": false} disables case lookup and inspector lists (retained workspace data stays available). The server and database keys of earlier releases are still accepted so an existing file keeps working, and are ignored. No password or connection string belongs in this file. Settings are revalidated for each request, including one that could use a cached list. The inspector list is kept for up to 30 minutes for the same shared folder and settings; Refresh inspector list and Try again read it fresh, and each inspector’s cases are always read fresh.

    The report helper waits up to 40 seconds for one case and 90 seconds for an open-case list. One case lookup and one list run at a time. A case answer over 1,000 rows, a list over 3,000 cases for one person or 200 inspectors, or a report answer over 20 MB fails without a partial import. Redirects are refused. Canceling a browser request suppresses its result.

    Data mapping and traceability

    The report’s XML export names each column after the report’s text box. A column whose value is empty in Accela (NULL) is left out of the export and is treated as blank. The case report’s definition is retained as tests/fixtures/reference/Document-Generator-Import.rdl and the open-case report’s as tests/fixtures/reference/OpenEnforcementCases_BI.rdl, for maintenance.

    Report column Import behavior
    CaseNumber Exact case identity, normalized to uppercase; a row for another case refuses the import
    SiteAddress Street address plus separately retained city/state/ZIP
    OwnerName / OwnerAddress Current owner and mailing address
    ParcelNumber Text, preserving leading zeros; existing formatting rules apply
    CaseDescription Imported as supplied
    HistoricDistrictName District name as the report prints it; when the report leaves it blank it is worked out from ZoningDistrict
    HistoricDistrict / IndividualLandmark Not printed by the report; worked out from ZoningDistrict with the report query’s own rules (HIS-MH, HIS-TL, HIS-UH, HIS-MB, HIS-FS; HIS-L). A Yes flag with a missing corresponding name blocks the import
    Landmark Retained for the existing landmark document checks
    InspectionDate / InspectionTime Completed inspection date and separate time; the time column is authoritative
    InspectionType / InspectionStatus / InspectorName Existing eligibility and roster checks
    RecordCategory Snow Removal selects the snow workflow
    DetailedDescription / ZoningDistrict Not retained in the imported case, as directed by the division

    Accepted case metadata includes accela.source: kind ssrs, the report server, the report path and the retrieval time. Cases imported by earlier releases keep their SQL provenance unchanged. Issued documents retain their frozen source facts. Refresh does not backdate or rewrite an issued document; use the correction workflow for changes to issued evidence. This is a read-only report integration, not an Accela upload or filing confirmation.

    City-network acceptance

    The supplied automated tests use synthetic report exports and a scripted PowerShell. The real report render, Windows sign-in, the report server’s certificate and City network access cannot be verified from the build environment.

    On a City PC, for at least two inspector accounts: load the inspector list and compare names and counts with the OpenEnforcementCases_BI report in the portal; open an inspector’s cases and compare them with the report run for that inspector; look up an ordinary case, a snow case and a case with a landmark or historic district and compare property, owner, parcel, historic/landmark fields, completed inspection date/time/status and inspector with DocumenGeneratorImport. Check off-network behavior (no VPN), an account without access to the reports, Refresh after closing a case in Accela, and that no console window flashes during a lookup. Keep test output out of operational case folders.

    Displayed code What to check
    SSRS_401 The report server did not accept the Windows sign-in. Confirm the person can open the report in the Reports portal.
    SSRS_403 The account may not run the report. Ask the report administrator for access to the Enforcement report folder.
    SSRS_404 The report was moved or renamed. Restore its path and name; the program reads fixed names.
    SSRS_500_rs... and other SSRS_<status> The report server could not run the report. The rs code is the report server’s own error name (for example rsInvalidReportParameter).
    SSRS_NETWORK City network or VPN, DNS and the report server’s availability.
    SSRS_TLS The report server’s certificate was not trusted by the PC.
    SSRS_REDIRECT The report server sent the request elsewhere; the program refuses redirects. Check the server address.
    SSRS_NOT_XML The answer is not valid UTF-8 report XML, or a web page came back instead of data (usually a sign-in or error page). Open the report in the portal on that PC and check its XML export.
    SSRS_DTD The XML contained a document type or entity declaration. The report data was refused; ask the report administrator to check the export.
    SSRS_LAYOUT A data row has an unexpected element name or namespace. Nothing was loaded; restore the report’s expected Details rows and column names.
    SSRS_WRONG_REPORT The XML came from a different report. The report’s name must stay exactly as above.
    SSRS_LIMIT The answer exceeded the size limits. Check the report for duplicate or unexpected rows.
    SCRIPT_POLICY Ask IT to approve the delivered helper under City policy. Do not bypass PowerShell policy.
    Script/helper returned no data Confirm the complete deployment is installed and PowerShell is permitted by City policy.

    After a failed lookup, %LOCALAPPDATA%\MadisonDocWriter\case-lookup-diagnostic.txt holds the full PowerShell error. It may name the server, the account or local paths; review it and send it only to IT. The next failed lookup replaces it.

    When the lookup is unavailable (not a City Windows computer, off the City network, disabled by the administrator, or the report cannot be run), no case can be imported until it is restored.

    Inspection identity and retained provenance

    The source query supplies no stable inspection ID. Within a case, the importer matches inspection type, actual date and normalized time; it never uses mutable status or owner details as identity. An initial inspection belongs to the case’s single original notice. Imported drafts, worksheets and issued snapshots retain importInspection as additive metadata. Historical documents/visits without that metadata use their stored inspection date/time; missing historical time conservatively blocks same-day reuse. Two known, different times remain distinct visits. Do not change an inspection’s time to work around a duplicate block; open the existing record and use correction when appropriate.

    Closed cases, existing drafts, pending issue confirmations, unreadable shared files and conflicting records do not start a new worksheet. Direct lookup rechecks shared history before confirmation. Failed checks leave existing work intact. The shared helper also rejects reuse of a retained imported inspection when publishing a visit.

    Approved server configuration

    The report server must appear in the ssrsHosts list of trusted-connections.json, which is part of the verified release. The shared folder cannot name another server. Ask the release owner to make any required change in a new release; inspectors must not alter it or bypass the refusal.

    Open cases by inspector (administrators)

    The helper lists the open enforcement cases assigned to each inspector from the OpenEnforcementCases_BI report, run with the signed-in Windows account. The report decides which cases are open (its current rule: record numbers starting CB, an assigned inspector, and a status that does not contain Close or Compliance and is not No Violation, Void or Withdrawn) and how each inspector is named. The helper counts each inspector’s distinct cases for the list and asks the report for one inspector’s cases by the name it printed.

    Four staff are always left off the inspector list because the division does not want them listed: Alice Duncan-Graves, Gregg May, Jessica Price and Phil Grupe (matched by name, so a middle initial or a spaced hyphen still matches). To keep people off the inspector list (supervisors or staff who do not do inspections), create Case Lookup/excluded-inspectors.json on the shared folder, using the supplied excluded-inspectors.example.json:

    {
  "exclude": [
    "Pat%Example",
    "ADMIN1"
  ]
}

    Each entry is a person’s display name or Accela user ID, matched without regard to case; % stands for any text, so Pat%Example also matches a middle name. Without the file, only the four fixed staff exclusions apply. An invalid file stops the list with a message naming it.

    20 Use keyboard touch and accessible views

    Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move through controls. Enter or Space activates the focused button or disclosure where appropriate. Visible focus identifies the active control. Click a validation link to open its section and move to the specific field; after correcting it, verify that the error state clears.

    Shortcut Scope and result
    ? Outside an editable field, opens keyboard help
    Ctrl+S or Cmd+S In Writer, requests device saving; verify its resulting status
    Escape Closes supported dialogs when no protected save is pending
    1, 2, 3, 4 In One item at a time, outside fields, selects Corrected, Progress made, No change or No access
    U Undoes the last result within the current worksheet context
    Tab or Shift+Tab Moves between controls; inside an open dialog, stays within it
    Enter or Space Activates the focused button
    Typing on a selected fill-in bubble Replaces the bubble with the detail you type
    Tab or Shift+Tab on a selected bubble Moves to the next or previous open fill-in bubble

    Held keys do not repeatedly result items. Typing a digit or U into an editable field remains ordinary text entry. Use the visible outcome controls for the same actions on touch devices.

    Read the whole task. Review all items provides an alternative to One item at a time. Reports provides tables alongside supported maps. Expand Full wording and guidance for complete language rather than depending on a truncated preview. Program instructions provides an accessible HTML manual as well as the printable copy.

    Small screens and zoom. The four Writer destinations remain available; open Import inspection from Workspace. On a narrow screen (760 CSS pixels or less) the document editor uses a compact header and one task bar at the bottom with the save state, Fix next issue, Review and the primary action; Review opens the Review dialog; the bar hides while you type in a field or a dialog is open and is never printed. Use vertical scrolling and the applicable table’s own scroll area when a wide data table needs it. On a phone-width screen the four destinations sit in two rows at the top. At high zoom, inspect the actual field labels and current action rather than relying on desktop positions. The HTML manual reflows at 320 CSS pixels and supports browser zoom and find.

    Display preferences. Select High contrast when useful, or Use device setting to follow the operating system preference. Reduced motion follows the browser setting. Printed issued documents have their own fixed layout; a screen theme does not change the historical body.

    Automated accessibility scans, theme checks, focus tests and narrow-width checks are included in the release evidence. They do not certify full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance. The City still needs manual screen-reader, keyboard, touch, zoom and real task testing with staff and its chosen assistive technology. Record the browser, screen reader, task, expected result and actual result in the acceptance record. Report a blocked control with its visible label and current case state, using synthetic records where possible.

    21 Troubleshoot common problems

    Preserve work first. Keep the active tab open when device saving is uncertain, download a workspace backup when offered, and record the exact message and time. The following actions do not require editing operational case files.

    Symptom Next action
    Shared program files failed verification Keep the installed verified version; give IT the message and time. Do not remove the pin or copy selected program files
    Open from the installed desktop shortcut Use the trusted installed shortcut in the original browser profile; preserve site data and unfinished work
    Helper session changed or request refused Reload to reconnect, then inspect the retained save state before retrying the original action
    GIS URL or report server refused IT checks the named setting against the connection allowlist in trusted-connections.json; do not weaken the check
    PDF contains an external resource or active element Preserve the issued original and report the error; use embedded approved document resources rather than external or local file references
    The case could not be exported Keep the case open and preserve the workspace backup if available; no empty case file should be written
    Report could not be sorted Default order is shown with a notice; review order before export and report the error if it repeats
    No eligible inspection results Review the inspection type, result status and displayed availability reason. Eligibility depends on both Inspection Type and Inspection Status. Scheduled, Pending, Completed, Inspection and No Violation results, Reinspection and No Fee Reinspection results on any inspection type other than a Reinspection, Initial Inspection results with No Entry, Assist inspections, undated rows and inspections already used on the case are not listed. Other combinations are listed as not available with their reason; use the type/status rules in chapter 4. If valid results are absent, use the complete current installation and retrieve the case again. An already used result requires Continue existing case
    An older version of Document Writer is still running Save your work and stop it: Exit Document Writer in Tools & settings when it offers one; otherwise close its command window or sign out of Windows and back in. Then double-click the Document Writer icon and confirm both versions match the install guide
    Exit Document Writer says work is still in progress Wait for the issuance, filing, email or save named in the message to finish, then choose Exit again; never close windows to force it
    Document Writer has stopped The program was stopped with Exit Document Writer. Close the window; double-click Document Writer on the desktop to start again
    A case is missing from Workspace Workspace shows all loaded cases. Use Import inspection to bring in a case from the City reports, or Open saved case for an exported case record
    Lookup finds only Scheduled or Assist records Confirm the source inspection was actually completed; use the division’s report procedure, not a fabricated date
    Report lookup error (SSRS_ code) Give IT the safe error code and time; check the City network or VPN, that the account can open the report in the Reports portal, and the report’s name and parameters
    Import says the inspection is already used Continue its retained case/document or use correction; do not change the time to bypass matching
    No language results Clear search; check the status scope. Approved language shows only entries with a recorded formal review, so switch to Approved and standard if you chose the narrower scope
    An unfilled bubble blocks issue Open the linked item, enter the actual missing detail and review the completed sentence
    Too many deadlines Review outstanding items and reduce to the permitted distinct dates; do not relabel compliance or withdrawal
    Deposit needs review or history changed Complete the affected charge and authorized source; refresh shared history and review the tier again
    Mandatory wording hold Preserve the draft; the division must supply approved defendant instructions for integration
    Save confirmation needed Confirm the original attempt; do not create another action
    This record was changed outside the program Stop editing; preserve evidence and refer to the administrator for trusted-source review
    Migration registry damaged Preserve the case folder and integrity evidence; IT reviews offline recovery
    PDF filing needed or filename conflict Open the issued action or PDF outbox; retain exact bytes and ask IT to resolve conflicting targets
    Report totals differ from expectation Check dates, active chips, definitions, read time and excluded summaries before requesting a rebuild
    Outlook did not send Inspect the draft and attachments and complete the actual send step; filing is not delivery

    For helper support, the current local structured log is %LOCALAPPDATA%.jsonl. A failed report lookup may also create case-lookup-diagnostic.txt in that program folder. Review logs before providing them to authorized IT; they may contain local paths, server or account details. The next lookup failure can replace its diagnostic file.

    If a control still fails after the safe next action, preserve the backup and error evidence. Ask the administrator to reproduce it with a copied or synthetic case. Do not retry by deleting registry, lock, receipt or history files. For save, connection and PDF states see chapter 14; for recovery, chapter 15.

    Earlier document formats

    Each issued document keeps the authoring version it was issued with. Its reprints and corrections use that format, and an unissued draft keeps its format unless an explicit adoption, such as Use simplified Reasons-only format, moves it to the current one. New documents use the current format described in chapters 5 to 13; new scoped orders (abatements, No Occupancy) keep authoring 13 because their layout is unchanged.

    Authoring version Best Interest and Vacancy Extensions Referrals and Compliance Letters
    11 and earlier Historical narrative layout, also for their corrections Historical layout; compliance letters list dates only
    12 Regular Extension layout; affected items listed in the details; a Vacancy Extension may be conditional (“Conditional — see conditions above”) and keeps its stored repair dates Historical layout
    13 Every affected item has a later due date in the items table; Vacancy Extensions are always dated. New Vacancy Extensions kept this format until authoring 16 Historical layout
    14 New Best Interest and Vacancy Extensions kept authoring 13 Referrals show item-specific inspection history and Days Outstanding; compliance letters list dates only
    15 Best Interest: Reasons with the explicit safety-exclusion confirmation and no signer Item history with notes in the history column; compliance letters add item history and Abate Yes/No
    16 (current) Every uncorrected item, no selection or safety confirmation and no signer; Best Interest takes the worksheet’s Next due dates; Vacancy prints no due date and needs a review inspection Notes print under the violation, corrected items included

    In the aligned table layout, authoring-12–15 Vacancy Extensions and authoring-12–14 Best Interest Extensions print their supervisory signer after the table; authoring-11 and earlier use their historical narrative layout. Ordinary Extensions keep their own stored authoring version; the special-extension column above describes only Best Interest and Vacancy Extensions. The authoring-11 initial citation packet may have six pages. Retain the original PDF for any document issued under a format an earlier release cannot render.

    The release package records technical verification and remaining City acceptance. Use the City acceptance record (Rnn-ACCEPTANCE-RECORD.md) to record the remaining City tests and approvals. Historical release reviews explain development provenance and do not override this manual.

    Current document summary

    New Best Interest and Vacancy Extensions cover every uncorrected item; new referral, referral-update and compliance documents print inspector notes under the violation; a referred case offers only Update for Case Referral or Compliance Letter. Compliance letters retain item-specific observation histories/notes and Abate values. Earlier issued documents keep their formats (Program instruction manual, chapter 22). New citation previews show all three copies by default; optional compact viewing never controls the final packet. Review actual regular and snow citation PDFs for all three distinct copies per new charge, and retain all four when reprinting an older four-copy packet.
